document_check.note: Faghfouri A, Shalchyan V, Toor HG, Amjad I, Niazi IK. A tensor decomposition scheme for EEG-based diagnosis of mild cognitive impairment. Heliyon 10 (2024) e26365, doi 10.1016/j.heliyon.2024.e26365. Dataset I is the Noor Hospital (Isfahan) resting-state 19-channel EEG set of 61 people over 55 (29 MCI, 32 healthy), taken from Ref. [24] (Kashefpour et al. 2019). Table 5 (p. 11) reports tensor-based accuracies of 82.13 (theta and alpha1), 83.37 (19 spectral features), 93.96 (60 frequency bands), 82.75 (Lempel-Ziv), 83.21 (Shannon entropy) and 68.89 (multi-scale sample entropy). These match the cited result. The block title in summaries.md (Paper 153) is this paper.

cited_result: Dataset I (Noor Hospital, Isfahan; 29 MCI / 32 HC), tensor-PARAFAC features with an RBF-kernel SVM, subject-wise random 41/20 train/test splits repeated three times, mean accuracy (Table 5, p. 11). Complexity features: Lempel-Ziv 82.75%, Shannon entropy 83.21%, multi-scale sample entropy 68.89%. Spectral features: theta+alpha1 band power 82.13%, 19 spectral features 83.37%, 60 micro-band power 93.96%.
tool_reason: The cited result is the classification accuracy of a machine-learning classifier (tensor features with an SVM) separating MCI from healthy controls, compared across feature sets. That is the performance and ranking of diagnostic prediction models, so PROBAST applies, with the PROBAST+AI considerations.

domains.rationale: Dataset I is a secondary two-group dataset (29 MCI, 32 healthy) from one hospital, taken from an earlier study. No sampling frame (consecutive or random enrolment) is described, so the design works as a diagnostic case-control comparison. Apart from age over 55 and at least primary education, no inclusion or exclusion criteria are reported, and recruitment details are deferred to Ref. [24].

signalling.question: 1.1 Were appropriate data sources used?
signalling.quote: In this study, the dataset in Ref. [24] has been used, which was recorded in Noor Hospital of Isfahan Province. The dataset includes 61 people over the age of 55,29 of them had MCI, and 32 of them were healthy.

signalling.question: 1.2 Were all inclusions and exclusions of participants appropriate?
signalling.quote: Searched Section 2.1.1 for exclusion criteria (neurological or psychiatric illness, medication, depression, recording-quality exclusions) and for how participants were recruited; none reported. The only stated criteria are age over 55 and 'All participants had primary or higher education.' [p. 3]; recruitment is deferred: 'For more descriptions of the recording details, please see Ref. [24].' [p. 3]

domains.rationale: The predictors are features computed algorithmically (band powers, entropies, Lempel-Ziv complexity, then PARAFAC components) from a 30-minute eyes-closed resting EEG recorded under one protocol for everyone. No manual reading is involved, and the EEG would be available at the time of intended use. Preprocessing was only channel normalisation and a 50 Hz notch filter, with no artefact rejection reported, but it was applied identically to all.

signalling.question: 2.1 Were predictors defined and assessed in a similar way for all participants?
signalling.quote: The EEG signals were recorded in the early morning for each person with their eyes closed and in a quiet room for 30 min.

signalling.question: 2.2 Were predictor assessments made without knowledge of outcome data?
signalling.quote: we filter the signals using a 4th degree Butterworth band pass filter and perform a Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) on these signals, and then the abs of signal power is calculated.

signalling.question: 2.3 Are all predictors available at the time the model is intended to be used?
signalling.quote: Moreover, a 19-channel EB-Neuro system whose electrodes were arranged according to a 10–20 standard was used to record the signal.

domains.rationale: MCI and healthy labels come from a psychiatric interview ('Patterson criteria', as printed), MMSE bands (21 to 26 for MCI, above 26 for healthy) and NUCOG confirmation (75 to 86.5). MMSE banding is crude and prone to misclassification. No functional or clinical-staging criterion is reported, and the interval between cognitive assessment and EEG is not stated. The outcome does not include the EEG predictors, and the test-based labels are unlikely to depend on the EEG.

signalling.quote: According to the psychiatric interview using Patterson criteria, all subjects were scored [p. 3]; (MMSE) score between 21 and 26 were classified as MCI patients. [p. 3]; Furthermore, people who scored above 26 are considered healthy [24]. [p. 3]

signalling.quote: In addition, to ensure the labeling of individuals, the Neuropsychiatry unit cognitive assessment tool (NUCOG) was used as the MCI diagnosis confirmation test, with scores between 75 and 86.5 being considered as MCI patients.

signalling.quote: Searched Sections 2.1.1 and 2.2 for the timing of the cognitive assessment relative to the EEG recording; not reported (recording details deferred to Ref. [24]).

domains.rationale: There are 29 MCI cases in total (20 per training set). The SVM is trained on 45 to 85 PARAFAC components, more than the 41 training participants. The configuration was tuned on the same splits used for testing: frequency segmentation, time-patch length and the number of components R were each chosen by best classification accuracy. There are only three random subject-wise hold-out splits, with no nested validation and no external validation for Dataset I. Only accuracy, sensitivity and specificity are reported, with no dispersion, confidence intervals, AUC or calibration, and no statistical comparison between feature sets. The reported metrics contain internal inconsistencies (see notes). The subject-level split, voting across patches, and fitting the PARAFAC decomposition on training data only are appropriate.

applicability.rationale: The sample is small, two-group and single-hospital (Isfahan), restricted to over-55s with at least primary education, and has no reported exclusion criteria.
The predictors come from a standard 19-channel 10-20 resting eyes-closed EEG, which is feasible in practice, although it needs a 30-minute recording (1.5-minute patches).
MCI is operationalised mainly by MMSE bands (21 to 26) with NUCOG confirmation. No functional criterion is reported.

overall_rationale: Domain 1 is high: a secondary two-group case-control dataset with no reported sampling frame or exclusion criteria. Domain 4 is high: 29 events, more components than training participants, hyperparameters and feature configuration tuned on test accuracy, three random splits only, no external validation, no dispersion or calibration, and internally inconsistent metrics. Domain 3 is unclear because of the MMSE-band outcome and the unstated timing. Any high domain makes the overall rating high.
